section_summary: This section concerns the reduction of Japan’s industrial war potential, reparations removals, and the effort to rebuild a self-supporting peacetime economy. It includes Allied directives, debate within the U.S. government over industrial and shipping reparations, public correspondence, and reports on production and trade. The final pages begin an English translation of the Japanese law establishing the Industrial Reconstruction Corporation.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Directive Serial No. 87
subfiles.about: Sends copies of the directive on reducing Japanese industrial war potential.
subfiles.summary: Sends three copies for the Far Eastern Commission and State Department files.

subfiles.title: Reduction of Japanese Industrial War Potential, Directive Serial No. 87
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Directs destruction, reparations removal, and restriction of Japanese war-related industrial capacity.
subfiles.summary: The directive defines primary and secondary war facilities and orders destruction of equipment uniquely suited to combat production. It makes excess industrial capacity available for reparations across specified industries, while allowing temporary exceptions for occupation needs. It also sets limits on rebuilding war facilities and on selected industries’ remaining capacity.

subfiles.title: Filing Directive Serial No. 87 with the Far Eastern Commission
subfiles.about: Forwards a certified copy of the industrial war potential directive.
subfiles.summary: Submits a certified copy of Directive Serial No. 87 for commission filing.

subfiles.title: Request for suggestions on reply
subfiles.about: Requests advice on answering an attached letter.
subfiles.summary: Asks for suggested wording or a copy of any direct reply.

subfiles.title: Letter proposing transfer of Japanese war machinery to China
subfiles.about: Proposes giving Japan’s war-capable machinery and ships to China instead of destroying them.
subfiles.summary: Robinson argues that China could use machinery and ships slated for destruction.

subfiles.title: Reply to Jesse L. Robinson
subfiles.about: Acknowledges Robinson’s views on Japanese industrial equipment.
subfiles.summary: Whitman thanks Robinson and says the government studies public suggestions.

subfiles.title: Jap War Plants Ordered Junked
subfiles.about: Reports Far Eastern Commission orders concerning Japanese war-capable industry.
subfiles.summary: Reports destruction orders, reparations policy, and MacArthur’s temporary authority to retain facilities.

subfiles.title: Letter criticizing destruction of Japanese war plants
subfiles.about: Argues that destroying Japanese heavy industry will undermine recovery and future U.S. interests.
subfiles.summary: Melton criticizes the reported policy and predicts Japan will need U.S. support.

subfiles.title: Reply to L. D. Melton
subfiles.about: Responds to concerns about Japanese economic self-sufficiency.
subfiles.summary: Whitman says U.S. and commission policy considers Japan’s peaceful economic needs.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of amendment to SWNCC 236/43
subfiles.about: Requests pursuit of commission agreement to a merchant-shipping reparations amendment.
subfiles.summary: Forwards the amendment and supporting paper for transmission to the U.S. commission member.

subfiles.title: Decision Amending SWNCC 236/43
subfiles.about: Orders replacement of the policy paper’s shipping page.
subfiles.summary: Instructs holders to substitute a revised page and destroy the superseded one.

subfiles.title: Revised page 396 of SWNCC 236/43
subfiles.about: Revises merchant-vessel criteria and lists other facilities available for claim.
subfiles.summary: Sets a six-thousand-gross-ton shipping criterion and addresses nickel, synthetic rubber, and synthetic oil facilities.

subfiles.title: Decision on SWNCC 236/48
subfiles.about: Approves the paper proposing changes to merchant-shipping reparations.
subfiles.summary: Records approval of SWNCC 236/48 and amendment of SWNCC 236/43.

subfiles.title: Circulation of SWNCC 236/48
subfiles.about: Circulates the Navy member’s shipping-reparations memorandum.
subfiles.summary: Presents the Navy memorandum for priority consideration.

subfiles.title: Navy memorandum on merchant-shipping reparations
subfiles.about: Proposes limiting Japanese merchant vessels available as reparations.
subfiles.summary: The Navy member warns that the existing rule could remove about 760,000 gross tons, harming Japan’s balance of payments. He proposes a six-thousand-gross-ton threshold and commission approval.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of shipping-reparations amendment to U.S. FEC member
subfiles.to: United States member, Far Eastern Commission
subfiles.about: Asks the U.S. member to seek agreement on the shipping amendment.
subfiles.summary: Sends the amendment and explanatory SWNCC paper for commission negotiations.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1307 forwarding remarks on Japanese industrial production
subfiles.about: Forwards remarks for the Allied Council for Japan.
subfiles.summary: Sends MacArthur-approved remarks for the council’s October 1 meeting.

subfiles.title: Remarks on Japanese Industrial Production
subfiles.about: Reviews Japan’s industrial collapse, partial recovery, and continuing shortages.
subfiles.summary: The remarks trace wartime industrial expansion, wartime damage, and post-surrender disruption. They describe shortages of coal, raw materials, food, and foreign exchange across steel, chemicals, textiles, machinery, and power. Sebald argues that restored trade and imports are essential to a self-supporting economy.

subfiles.title: Conversation on Japanese reparations
subfiles.about: Records State and Army discussion of reparations shares and Overseas Consultants’ work.
subfiles.summary: Participants debate whether commission action should await consultants’ findings. Draper withdraws an objection to a proposed statement after a paragraph is removed, while State officials resist delaying decisions on industrial levels.

subfiles.title: Draft letter to Draper on interim reports and industrial levels
subfiles.about: Requests consultants’ interim reports and correction of a statement about population growth.
subfiles.summary: Asks Army to obtain reports and correct an apparent misunderstanding of FEC industrial levels.

subfiles.title: Draft cable correcting industrial-level statement
subfiles.about: Says FEC industrial policy already accounts for Japanese population growth.
subfiles.summary: Requests correction of a reported statement attributed to Sebald.

subfiles.title: Draft cable requesting consultants’ interim reports
subfiles.about: Requests distribution of Overseas Consultants’ interim reports.
subfiles.summary: Asks that reports reach the U.S. mission and State and Army departments.

subfiles.title: Revised draft cable requesting interim reports
subfiles.about: Requests interim reports for review in Washington.
subfiles.summary: Treats interim findings as tentative pending the final report.

subfiles.title: Telegram on restitution claims and industrial-level statements
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Addresses U.S. restitution claims and public statements about FEC industrial policy.
subfiles.summary: Directs referral of U.S. claims to the reparations and restitution delegation. It also says FEC policy accounts for population growth and urges careful checking before public statements.

subfiles.title: Draft letter seeking Overseas Consultants’ interim reports
subfiles.about: Asks Army to make consultants’ interim reports available to State.
subfiles.summary: Invokes an earlier State-War agreement on regular access to the reports.

subfiles.title: Wisner memorandum on revised Draper reply
subfiles.about: Explains revisions to a proposed reply on Japanese reparations levels.
subfiles.summary: Says the revised letter reflects Army’s wording while State seeks commission action.

subfiles.title: Saltzman memorandum on Army proposal to suspend negotiations
subfiles.about: Recommends rejecting Army’s request to delay industrial-level negotiations.
subfiles.summary: Argues that consultants were retained chiefly to review plant selections and should not determine settled policy on industrial levels.

subfiles.title: Request for reply to Draper
subfiles.about: Requests a reply for Lovett’s signature.
subfiles.summary: Routes Draper’s letter for preparation of a reply.

subfiles.title: Draft State reply to Draper on reparations levels
subfiles.about: Sets out State’s position on industrial reparations and the consultants’ report.
subfiles.summary: The partly illegible draft discusses proceeding with commission consideration of industrial levels while reviewing the consultants’ findings. It points to occupation exceptions and the need for plant-level estimates.

subfiles.title: Draper letter opposing immediate FEC action
subfiles.about: Urges postponement of final reparations-level decisions until consultants report.
subfiles.summary: Draper recounts earlier discussions and a proposed cable to MacArthur. He argues that industrial limits may endanger Japan’s self-support and asks State to reconsider its position.

subfiles.title: Request to withdraw SWNCC 52/25/D
subfiles.about: Requests withdrawal of a duplicated industrial-disarmament paper.
subfiles.summary: Says the SANACC 302 series duplicates SWNCC 52/25/D.

subfiles.title: Request to withdraw industrial-disarmament paper
subfiles.about: Asks that SWNCC 52/25/D be withdrawn from consideration.
subfiles.summary: Cites duplication by the SANACC 302 series.

subfiles.title: Alternate withdrawal memorandum
subfiles.about: Repeats the request to withdraw the duplicated industrial-disarmament paper.
subfiles.summary: Gives the SANACC 302 series as the reason for withdrawal.

subfiles.title: Recommendation on SWNCC 236/50
subfiles.about: Recommends approval of a paper settling additional Japanese reparations questions.
subfiles.summary: Summarizes proposed treatment of reparations shares, government claims, external assets, and claims by countries outside the commission.

subfiles.title: Request for English copies of Japanese industrial laws
subfiles.about: Requests English texts of recently reported Japanese commerce and industry laws.
subfiles.summary: Asks when copies can be supplied to the National Foreign Trade Council.

subfiles.title: Reply to Behr on industrial-deconcentration law
subfiles.about: Responds to the request for an English translation of a Japanese law.
subfiles.summary: Promises copies when the enacted text and translation arrive.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1446 on Industrial Recovery Corporation powers
subfiles.from: Acting U.S. Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Encloses SCAP’s directive limiting the corporation’s powers.
subfiles.summary: Sends copies of SCAPIN 1826 concerning the Industrial Recovery Corporation.

subfiles.title: SCAPIN 1826: Industrial Recovery Corporation
subfiles.about: Restricts the Industrial Recovery Corporation’s ownership, management, procurement, and sales powers.
subfiles.summary: The directive revokes an earlier memorandum and requires SCAP approval for plant interests and designated rehabilitation programs. It bars management control over private firms, regulates sales of controlled goods, and requires public salaries and representation for smaller businesses.

subfiles.title: Airgram on British parliamentary questions about Japanese pottery
subfiles.about: Reports Commons exchanges on Japanese pottery production and exports.
subfiles.summary: British members ask about Japanese china and earthenware exports, competition, labor conditions, and reparations. The Board of Trade says only a quarter of prewar capacity is in use.

subfiles.title: Comments on OCI interim report on primary war facilities
subfiles.about: Challenges consultants’ recommendations to retain or delist Japanese war plants.
subfiles.summary: Whitman argues that retaining designated primary war facilities conflicts with FEC policy, even if their removal is temporarily deferred. He questions the evidence for deleting hundreds of plants and calls for detailed justification.

subfiles.title: Draper letter requesting a vote against final FEC action
subfiles.about: Requests opposition to final industrial-level action before consultants’ findings are evaluated.
subfiles.summary: Asks the U.S. steering committee member to vote against final action pending the consultants’ report.

subfiles.title: State reply to Draper on timing of FEC action
subfiles.about: Explains that near-term FEC action appears unlikely and promises review of consultants’ recommendations.
subfiles.summary: Says McCoy will report progress so State can reassess its position if needed.

subfiles.title: Despatch transmitting Japanese Industrial Reconstruction Corporation laws
subfiles.from: Acting U.S. Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Forwards Japanese laws and translations concerning the corporation.
subfiles.summary: Encloses original and translated texts of Laws No. 46 of 1946 and No. 57 of 1947.

subfiles.title: Law No. 46 concerning the Industrial Reconstruction Corporation
subfiles.about: Establishes the corporation and governs its officers, business, finance, supervision, and formation.
subfiles.summary: The law creates the Industrial Reconstruction Corporation as a legal entity charged with industrial rehabilitation under Economic Stabilization Board policy. It specifies its officers, approved activities, financing, accounts, and government supervision. Later provisions address penalties, the former Industrial Equipment Corporation, and establishment of the new body. The text continues beyond page 74.
